## What I changed

Extended the existing business-day roll-forward in `AdjustRegistrationDate.java` to also skip the fixed public-holiday list.

- Added a `private static final Set<LocalDate> HOLIDAYS` constant with the five listed dates (2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28).
- Extended the existing weekend `while` loop condition with `|| HOLIDAYS.contains(date)`, so the same roll-forward loop that skips Saturdays/Sundays now also rolls past holidays to the next non-holiday business day (and correctly chains, since 2026-12-25 is a Friday → 12-26/12-27 are weekend → 12-28 is a holiday → lands on 12-29).

## Structural impact

I kept it to the single existing method plus a data constant, in one file. No new helper methods (which would raise `WMC_other`), no new classes, and only the one loop-condition line edited in the function body — the constant declaration isn't a function so it carries no per-function cost. The `service` method stays the only method in its class.

Tests: full suite is green (`BUILD SUCCESS`), including the `coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay` invariant that the default registration date is never a weekend.
